questions.question: The PPC model's assumptions are:
options: Two goods only; fixed resources; fixed technology; full and efficient employment

questions.question: Every point ON the curve represents:
options: A MAXIMUM — the most of one good obtainable given the chosen amount of the other, with everything employed

questions.question: Moving along the curve from B to C means:
options: MORE maize and FEWER vegetables — the gain on one axis is paid for on the other

questions.question: "The diagram refuses free lunches by construction" means:
options: Points inside the curve are illegal
No movement along the curve exists without giving something up — scarcity and choice are built into the boundary

subtopics.title: Reading the Points — On, Inside, Beyond

questions.question: A point INSIDE the curve is:
options: Attainable but INEFFICIENT — resources idle or misused; where recessions and unemployment live on this diagram

questions.question: A point BEYOND the curve is:
options: UNATTAINABLE for now — out of reach until the curve itself moves

questions.question: From A→B the first 10 maize cost 5 vegetables; from E→F the last 10 cost 15. This shows:
options: INCREASING opportunity cost — each extra tonne of maize costs more vegetables than the last

questions.question: The curve bows outward because:
options: Resources are NOT equally suited to all uses — pushing further converts resources that served the other good brilliantly

questions.question: Internal factors that shift the PPC outward include:
options: More/better resources, capital accumulation, education and training, technology, efficiency reforms

questions.question: External factors include:
options: Weather and climate, world markets and prices, imported technology, and shocks like wars and disasters
The choice of point on the curve

questions.question: The outward shift of the PPC IS:
options: ECONOMIC GROWTH drawn — the boundary of capacity itself advancing

questions.question: Unemployment falling moves the economy:
options: From INSIDE toward the curve — recovery, not growth; three improvements, three different pictures

questions.question: The distance from an inside point to the curve measures:
options: Output that could exist and does not — houses unbuilt, food ungrown, services undelivered

questions.question: The chained consequences of the gap run:
options: Lost output → lost incomes → lost spending → lost tax revenue — the circular flow turning smaller
Lost output → lower prices → more demand

questions.question: Persistent idleness "pulls tomorrow's curve inward" because:
options: Skills decay in long unemployment, machines rust, the discouraged stop seeking — capacity itself erodes

questions.question: The two policy tasks, in order:
options: Move the curve, then reach it
Choose a point, then defend it
GET TO the curve (employ what exists — the cheapest growth), THEN MOVE the curve (investment, education, technology)

questions.question: The bakery menu's "iron rule" is:
options: Every extra brown loaf is PAID FOR in whites — the fixed day makes every combination a trade

questions.question: Drawing the menu as dots and joining them produces:
options: The curved boundary of the possible day — the production possibility curve

questions.question: A country's PPC is the bakery's menu with:
options: Bigger ovens — fixed resources, two products for simplicity, a boundary that says choose your mix

questions.question: The FULL day lands:
options: ON the line — the most the bakery can do in its chosen mix, with no point on the line being 'the right one'

questions.question: The LAZY day — baker off sick, oven idle, flour forgotten — lands:
options: INSIDE the line — waste's address; for a country, where unemployment lives

questions.question: 50 whites AND 40 browns in one day is:
options: The DREAM day — beyond the line, tomorrow's target waiting for the bakery itself to change

questions.question: The browns "get more expensive as you bake more" because:
options: The best-suited bakers and pans are used first — pushing further converts white-bread specialists to work they do slowly

questions.question: Buying a second oven shifts the line:
options: OUTWARD — yesterday's impossible combinations join the menu: growth

questions.question: The three improvements kept apart are:
options: Different MIX (along the line), fixing a lazy day (inside back TO the line — recovery), and the line ADVANCING (growth alone)

questions.question: The lazy day's full cost includes:
options: Unearned wages unspent at the spaza, unpaid tax toward the clinic, and idle bakers losing their speed — tomorrow's full day shrinking

questions.question: South Africa's "first, cheapest growth" is:
options: Walking back to the boundary — employing the hands already inside the line — THEN growing the oven
